selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline: sshd healthy, host cert configured and active
selected_evidence.summary: sshd -t passed, service restarted/started, and sshd -T showed hostcertificate active before the node restart; boot_id 272eff4c-5c0e-4adb-8653-6b4d70d5e553 recorded as baseline.

selected_evidence.requirement: CA created and host certificate correctly signed
selected_evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated the CA at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca and signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub into ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1, 10.100.115.10, localhost, valid forever; ssh-keygen -L confirmed the cert structure and signing CA fingerprint.

selected_evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects without host-key prompting
selected_evidence.summary: With UserKnownHostsFile containing only an @cert-authority entry for the CA pubkey, ssh -vv showed 'Host key verification... is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' and proceeded to auth (Permission denied on pubkey/password, i.e. host verification succeeded); a client with neither CA trust nor a pinned key instead got 'Host key verification failed', isolating the CA as the trust source.
`sudo -n reboot` was launched via nohup/disown in the background and the exec call returned 'reboot_issued' successfully before the connection dropped on the next poll.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Repeated polling after issuing the reboot showed connection resets/timeouts (node down/rebooting), then exec access returned with boot_id f9af7005-7ab3-485c-b97e-097a8812e2e1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id 272eff4c-5c0e-4adb-8653-6b4d70d5e553, proving an actual OS restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sshd, host certificate config, and CA-based trust behavior
selected_evidence.summary: After the restart, rc-service sshd status showed 'started', sshd -T still listed the HostCertificate path, ssh-keygen -L re-confirmed the cert, and the CA-only known_hosts client test again showed 'is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' followed by auth-stage denial, proving the certificate-based trust setup survived and functions after the restart.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 1: create CA key =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /etc/ssh/ca
if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca ]; then
  sudo -n ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca -N '' -C "ssh-host-ca@$NODE_NAME"
fi
sudo -n chmod 600 /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca
sudo -n chmod 644 /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca.pub
echo "CA pubkey:"; sudo -n cat /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca.pub

echo "== STEP 2: sign host ed25519 pubkey =="
HOSTNAMES="$NODE_NAME,$NODE_IP,localhost"
sudo -n ssh-keygen -s /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca -I "host_${NODE_NAME}" -h -n "$HOSTNAMES" -V always:forever /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
sudo -n chmod 644 /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
echo "Cert info:"
sudo -n ssh-keygen -L -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub

echo "== STEP 3: configure sshd to present cert =="
if ! grep -q '^HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' /etc/ssh/sshd_config; then
  printf '\nHostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub\n' | sudo -n tee -a /etc/ssh/sshd_config >/dev/null
fi
sudo -n sshd -t
echo "== STEP 4: restart sshd (config reload, not node restart) =="
sudo -n rc-service sshd restart
sleep 1
sudo -n rc-service sshd status

echo "== STEP 5: distribute CA pub for client trust =="
sudo -n cp /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca.pub /tmp/ssh_host_ca.pub
sudo -n chmod 644 /tmp/ssh_host_ca.pub
echo DONE

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== build known_hosts trusting the CA only (no pinned host key) =="
CA_PUB="$(cat /tmp/ssh_host_ca.pub)"
printf '@cert-authority %s,%s,localhost %s\n' "$NODE_NAME" "$NODE_IP" "$CA_PUB" > /tmp/ca_known_hosts
cat /tmp/ca_known_hosts

echo "== connect with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, using ONLY the CA-trust known_hosts =="
ssh -vv -o UserKnownHostsFile=/tmp/ca_known_hosts -o GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 \
    -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PasswordAuthentication=[REDACTED]]] \
    root@"$NODE_IP" true 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'certificate|Server host key|Host key verification|Authenticated to|Permission denied|debug1: Host' \
  || true
echo "exit_marker=done"

echo "== sanity: without CA trust and without pinned key, host key verification should FAIL (proves cert is what grants trust) =="
rm -f /tmp/empty_known_hosts; touch /tmp/empty_known_hosts
ssh -o UserKnownHostsFile=/tmp/empty_known_hosts -o GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 \
    root@"$NODE_IP" true 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'Host key verification failed|no matching host key' || echo "unexpected_result"
